senses.gloss: To choose to do something, especially in a formal or official situation.
examples: She *elected* to take the earlier flight.
Employees may *elect* to receive the bonus as stock.
Having *elected* to represent himself, he lost the case.

senses.gloss: To get rid of something completely.
examples: The new process *eliminates* most of the paperwork.
We *eliminated* sugar from her diet.
That bug has been *eliminated* in the latest update.

senses.gloss: To fix something firmly into a surrounding material or surface.
senses.ru: вставлять, вделывать, закреплять (внутри чего-л.); застревать, засесть
examples: A piece of glass was *embedded* in his heel.
The bullet *embedded* itself in the door frame.
Workers *embed* steel bars in the concrete before it sets.

senses.gloss: To make a story more interesting by adding details that are not true.
examples: He always *embellishes* the story a little.
She *embellished* her résumé and got caught.
The tale has been *embellished* with every retelling.

senses.gloss: To use a method, a skill, or a tool for a purpose.
examples: The team *employs* several different testing methods.
Doctors *employed* a new technique to close the wound.
The film is *employing* the same trick for the third time.

senses.gloss: To make someone feel confident and in control of their own life.
senses.ru: давать уверенность в своих силах, расширять возможности
examples: Learning to drive *empowered* her.
Good teachers *empower* students to think for themselves.
She felt *empowered* after the first week of classes.

senses.gloss: To flow into a larger body of water, said of a river or a stream.
examples: The Mississippi *empties* into the Gulf of Mexico.
Two small streams *emptied* into the lake behind the house.
The canal *emptying* into the harbor was dug in 1830.

senses.gloss: To try to do as well as someone you admire by copying the way they do things.
examples: Younger players try to *emulate* his footwork.
She *emulated* her older sister in everything.
He has spent years *emulating* his father's work ethic.

senses.gloss: To make it possible for someone to do something.
senses.ru: давать возможность, дать возможность; позволять, позволить
examples: The scholarship *enabled* him to finish college.
A small loan will *enable* us to open a second store.
The new bridge has *enabled* farmers to reach the market in an hour.

senses.gloss: To put a magic spell on someone or something.
examples: The witch *enchanted* the mirror so that it would answer her.
In the story, a wizard *enchants* the sword.
The forest had been *enchanted* long before they arrived.

senses.gloss: To surround an area with a wall, a fence, or a border.
examples: A low stone wall *encloses* the garden.
They *enclosed* the yard so the dog could run.
The pool is *enclosed* by a tall fence.

senses.gloss: To give someone a quality or an ability by nature, usually in the passive.
examples: Nature *endowed* him with a remarkable memory.
She is *endowed* with enormous patience.
Good soil can *endow* a wine with real character.

senses.gloss: To fit together and lock into place, said of a mechanical part.
senses.ru: включаться, входить в зацепление; включать (передачу, тормоз)
examples: Make sure the parking brake is *engaged*.
The gears *engage* with a soft click.
The lock *engaged* as soon as the door swung shut.

senses.gloss: To have something good and benefit from it.
examples: At eighty he still *enjoys* excellent health.
The restaurant *enjoyed* a long run of good reviews.
The company has *enjoyed* record profits for three years.

senses.gloss: To have guests in your home and give them food and drink.
examples: They *entertain* a lot during the holidays.
We *entertained* twelve people on Thanksgiving.
She has been *entertaining* clients all week.

senses.gloss: To consider an idea or an offer seriously.
examples: The board refused to *entertain* the offer.
He briefly *entertained* the idea of moving to Alaska.
She has never *entertained* the thought of quitting.

senses.gloss: To give a book, a film, or a piece of music a particular title.
examples: She *entitled* the book "Small Hours".
He read a poem *entitled* "November".
What do you plan to *entitle* the last chapter?

senses.gloss: To be the same in amount, size, or value as something else.
examples: Two plus two *equals* four.
Three teaspoons *equal* one tablespoon.
Last year's losses *equaled* everything we had saved.

senses.gloss: To make amounts or conditions the same as each other.
examples: The valve *equalizes* the pressure between the two tanks.
The new formula *equalized* school funding across the state.
Divers wait for their ears to *equalize* before going deeper.

senses.gloss: To pass a problem to someone with more authority so that it gets solved.
examples: If the agent can't help, ask her to *escalate* the ticket.
I *escalated* the complaint to a supervisor.
The case has been *escalated* to the legal department.

senses.gloss: To find out a fact and prove it beyond doubt.
examples: The autopsy *established* the cause of death.
We need to *establish* who was in the building that night.
It has been *established* that the fire started in the kitchen.

senses.gloss: To avoid dealing with a duty, a payment, or a question that you should face.
senses.ru: уклоняться, уклониться (от уплаты, от ответа); увиливать
examples: He *evaded* every question about the money.
She was charged with *evading* taxes for six years.
Don't *evade* the issue.

senses.gloss: To leave something out so that it is not part of a total or a set.
senses.ru: не включать, исключать (из суммы, из перечня)
examples: The price *excludes* tax and tip.
The first estimate *excluded* labor costs.
Meals are *excluded* from the package.

senses.gloss: To carry out a plan, an order, or a task.
examples: The team *executed* the play perfectly.
Someone has to *execute* the plan, not just write it.
The order was *executed* within the hour.

senses.gloss: To use a right, a power, or a quality that you have.
examples: Please *exercise* caution on the icy steps.
She *exercised* her right to remain silent.
The governor has rarely *exercised* the veto.

senses.gloss: To apply force, pressure, or influence on something.
examples: The moon *exerts* a pull on the oceans.
Her father *exerted* enormous influence over the company.
Pressure is being *exerted* on the mayor to resign.

senses.gloss: To show a feeling, a quality, or a symptom clearly.
examples: The patient *exhibited* all the classic symptoms.
Young children often *exhibit* fear of strangers.
He has never *exhibited* the slightest interest in money.

senses.gloss: To require something of someone because you consider it their duty.
examples: The school *expects* students to be in their seats by eight.
You are *expected* to answer emails within a day.
We *expected* better manners from a grown man.

senses.gloss: To force air, liquid, or gas out of something.
examples: The whale *expelled* a spout of water.
Cough hard to *expel* the water from your lungs.
Air is *expelled* through a vent at the back.

senses.gloss: To increase suddenly and very quickly in number or amount.
examples: The city's population *exploded* in the 1990s.
Demand for the toy has *exploded* since Christmas.
Costs *explode* once you add a second warehouse.

senses.gloss: To suddenly show violent anger.
examples: He *exploded* when he saw the bill.
Don't *explode* at the kids over a broken glass.
She had never *exploded* like that in a meeting before.
